$comment: EXP-1798 (2026-11-12, after a tool-test script hard-deleted 16 prod issues by looping a delete over a list result): THE GUARD RAILS ON EVERY DESTRUCTIVE OP of Exponential's MCP surface (`/api/mcp`). DESTRUCTIVE OPS (`destructiveOps`: noun -> op -> the ONE argument that names what goes) are every op that deletes, trashes or revokes, on whichever wire tool carries it (`exponential_<noun>_write`, or the noun's own name for a first-party caller's legacy writes). ONE EXPLICIT ID (`singleId`, `singleIdCases`): the named argument must be ONE string, trimmed non-empty, at most `maxIdLength` chars, holding none of `forbiddenChars` (whitespace, `,`, `;`, `*`, `[`, `]`): no arrays, no lists, no wildcards, no filters; anything else is refused before the op's handler runs with `errors.notOne` (absent: `errors.missing`). Not checkable server-side: whether the caller (an agent) took the id from the user or from a list result; so the rule is in words (`descriptionLine` appended to the description of every tool that carries a destructive op, `instructionsLine` in the server instructions) and bounded by THE BURST GUARD (`burst`, `burstCases`): per caller key (`burstKey`: the caller's own verified session `session:<id>` when the request runs inside one, else the credential `user:<userId>|token:<first 16 hex of SHA-256 of the Authorization header, or cookie>`), at most `burst.max` destructive calls are ADMITTED within any `burst.windowSeconds` (a sliding window over admitted calls only; a refused call does not extend it). The next one is refused with `errors.burst` (`{max}`, `{window}` filled in) and audited `failed` / `deleteBurst`. The FIRST refusal per key within a window posts `burst.event` to the team stream (emitted by the server; `eventPayload` keys; team = the session's team, else the one team a confined credential reaches, else the caller's personal team); further refusals in that window stay quiet (`blockedQuiet`). The payload never names the id (the stream is the whole team's, and the refused id may be another team's); the audit row does. Defaults hold for normal use (a person deletes one thing at a time); `burst.env` overrides them per deployment (positive integers; anything else = the default). Counting is per server process. AUDIT: every destructive call's `mcp_calls` row (audit.json) carries `session_id` (the caller's verified session, else null) and `target` = `<op>:<id>` (`destructiveTarget`, `targetCases`: the id as sent, cut to `maxIdLength`; a non-string id = `<op>:?`; any other call = null), so token (`client_id` / `user_id`), session and the deleted id are on the row. TOOL TESTS (the repo's MCP harnesses: `apps/web/scripts/mcp-oauth-e2e.mjs` and any script with `--base` / `--bearer`) default to a local stack and refuse a `prodHosts` base unless `prodFlag` is given (`prodHostCases`).

errors.notOne: {noun}.{op} takes exactly ONE explicit {key} the user named: no lists, arrays, wildcards or filters.
errors.burst: Refused: more than {max} deletes within {window} s by this caller. Delete only ids the user named, one per call; never loop a delete over a list result. Ask the user before deleting more.

descriptionLine: Never delete ids from a list result.
instructionsLine: Delete only an id the user named, one per call; never act on a list result.

burstCases.name: the window slides over admitted calls
